sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ: both get 401 with the login page and "Invalid email or password", same status, text and timing (bcrypt runs against a dummy hash for unknown emails).
sonnet.q2: The email is locked: every attempt gets 429 with Retry-After (seconds until locked_until) and the "Too many failed attempts" login page, with no password check (even the correct password is blocked) for 15 minutes. Refused attempts aren't counted and don't extend the lock. Cookie untouched.
sonnet.q3: On a successful login, the session the incoming cookie points to is deleted in the same transaction that inserts the new session (new random ID, new cookie set). A failed login leaves the old session and cookie untouched.
sonnet.q4: Only the opaque random session ID (256 random bits, base64url, 43 chars) with no user data. Page scripts cannot read it because the cookie is HttpOnly (also Secure, SameSite=Lax, __Host-sid).
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (the absolute limit, never extended), since the 30-minute idle expiry keeps being refreshed. The user is then sent 303 to /login.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE matches zero rows, so the server responds 303 redirect to /login and clears the cookie (Cache-Control: no-store). No protected content is served.
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the session row (matching the SHA-256 hash of the cookie) before responding; then 303 to /login with the cookie cleared. If the session is already gone (none found), that still counts as success with the same result; with no or malformed cookie it also returns 303 /login and clears the cookie. If the database errors, 503 and the cookie is kept.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres database's sessions table, keyed by the SHA-256 hash of the cookie value. Either instance looks it up by that primary key with the UPDATE ... WHERE id_hash = $1 statement, so no sticky sessions are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table (email, failed_at stamped with clock_timestamp()). The window is an exact sliding one: count rows for that email where failed_at > clock_timestamp() - 10 minutes, including the new failure; no fixed buckets.
sonnet.q10: It compares idle_expires_at and absolute_expires_at against the database now(), both must be in the future, for the row with matching id_hash. If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and idle_expires_at = least(now() + 30 minutes, absolute_expires_at), in one UPDATE ... RETURNING user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 with the login page "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly." The transaction is rolled back, no session is created, and no Set-Cookie is sent (cookie untouched).
sonnet.q12: The cleanup job, run every 5 minutes, deletes sessions WHERE idle_expires_at <= now() (which also covers the absolute limit). Correctness doesn't depend on it because expired rows are rejected at check time.
